name: Ronin Bridge
tldr: Withdrawals needed 5 of 9 validator signatures. Attackers got 5 private keys and signed the withdrawals themselves. Nobody noticed for six days.
what: Ronin was the blockchain behind the game Axie Infinity, with a bridge that needed 5 of 9 validators to approve withdrawals.
happened: Attackers, later attributed by the FBI to North Korea's Lazarus Group, gained control of 5 validator keys and approved two huge withdrawals: 173,600 ETH and 25.5M USDC.
bug: No code bug. Too few keys, too concentrated: four of the nine were run by the same company, so one more key was enough.
prevent: More independent signers, hardware security, monitoring of large withdrawals, and alerts that someone actually watches.
lesson: Perfect code still fails if the keys are weak. Security includes people and operations.
